import Mathlib

inductive BinarySearchTree : Type
| Empty : BinarySearchTree
| Node : Int → BinarySearchTree → BinarySearchTree → BinarySearchTree
deriving Inhabited

def view (t : BinarySearchTree) : Set Int :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Empty => ∅
  | BinarySearchTree.Node v l r => view l ∪ view r ∪ {v}

def is_bst (t : BinarySearchTree) : Prop :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Empty => True
  | BinarySearchTree.Node v l r =>
    (∀ x ∈ view l, x < v) ∧
    is_bst l ∧
    (∀ x ∈ view r, x > v) ∧
    is_bst r

def get_left (t : BinarySearchTree) : Option BinarySearchTree :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Node _ l _ => some l
  | _ => none

def get_right (t : BinarySearchTree) : Option BinarySearchTree :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Node _ _ r => some r
  | _ => none

def get_val (t : BinarySearchTree) : Option Int :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Node v _ _ => some v
  | _ => none

def BinarySearchTree.is_node (t : BinarySearchTree) : Prop :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Node _ _ _ => True
  | _ => False

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def zig_precond (t : BinarySearchTree) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  is_bst t ∧ 
  BinarySearchTree.is_node t ∧ 
  (match get_left t with | some l => BinarySearchTree.is_node l | none => False)
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def zig (t : BinarySearchTree) 
    (h_precond : zig_precond t) : BinarySearchTree :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Node v (BinarySearchTree.Node lv ll lr) r =>
      BinarySearchTree.Node lv ll (BinarySearchTree.Node v lr r)
  | _ => t
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def zig_postcond (t : BinarySearchTree) (result : BinarySearchTree)
    (_ : zig_precond t) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  is_bst result ∧
  view result = view t ∧
  -- Structural properties
  get_val result = get_val (get_left t).get! ∧
  BinarySearchTree.is_node (get_right result).get! ∧
  get_val (get_right result).get! = get_val t
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem zig_postcond_satisfied (t : BinarySearchTree)
    (h_precond : zig_precond t) :
    zig_postcond t (zig t h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  rcases t with _ | ⟨v, l, r⟩
  · simp [zig_precond, BinarySearchTree.is_node] at h_precond
  · rcases l with _ | ⟨lv, ll, lr⟩
    · simp [zig_precond, BinarySearchTree.is_node, get_left] at h_precond
    ·
      have hbst := h_precond.1
      change
        (∀ x ∈ view (BinarySearchTree.Node lv ll lr), x < v) ∧
        is_bst (BinarySearchTree.Node lv ll lr) ∧
        (∀ x ∈ view r, x > v) ∧
        is_bst r at hbst
      rcases hbst with ⟨hLeft, hLeftBst, hRight, hRightBst⟩

      change
        (∀ x ∈ view ll, x < lv) ∧
        is_bst ll ∧
        (∀ x ∈ view lr, x > lv) ∧
        is_bst lr at hLeftBst
      rcases hLeftBst with
        ⟨hLL, hLLBst, hLRAbove, hLRBst⟩

      have hLRBelow : ∀ x ∈ view lr, x < v := by
        intro x hx
        apply hLeft x
        simp [view, hx]

      have hRootOrder : lv < v := by
        apply hLeft lv
        simp [view]

      have hRotatedBst :
          is_bst
            (BinarySearchTree.Node lv ll
              (BinarySearchTree.Node v lr r)) := by
        change
          (∀ x ∈ view ll, x < lv) ∧
          is_bst ll ∧
          (∀ x ∈ view (BinarySearchTree.Node v lr r), x > lv) ∧
          is_bst (BinarySearchTree.Node v lr r)
        refine ⟨hLL, hLLBst, ?_, ?_⟩
        · intro x hx
          simp only [view, Set.mem_union, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hx
          rcases hx with (hx | hx) | rfl
          · exact hLRAbove x hx
          · exact lt_trans hRootOrder (hRight x hx)
          · exact hRootOrder
        · change
            (∀ x ∈ view lr, x < v) ∧
            is_bst lr ∧
            (∀ x ∈ view r, x > v) ∧
            is_bst r
          exact ⟨hLRBelow, hLRBst, hRight, hRightBst⟩

      unfold zig_postcond
      constructor
      · simpa [zig] using hRotatedBst
      constructor
      · change
          view
              (BinarySearchTree.Node lv ll
                (BinarySearchTree.Node v lr r)) =
            view
              (BinarySearchTree.Node v
                (BinarySearchTree.Node lv ll lr) r)
        ext x
        simp only [view, Set.mem_union, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
        tauto
      · simp [zig, get_val, get_left, get_right,
          BinarySearchTree.is_node]
  -- !benchmark @end proof

A single right rotation transforms

`Node v (Node lv ll lr) r`

into

`Node lv ll (Node v lr r)`.

The proof extracts the ordering conditions from the original BST invariant. In particular, every element of `lr` is below `v`, `lv < v`, and every element of `r` is above `v`. These facts establish the invariant for the new right subtree and then for the rotated tree. Set preservation follows by extensionality and rearranging unions.

analysis:
The student’s submission appears to satisfy the semantic requirements of the problem.

What the problem requires:
1. Implement a BST-like tree structure.
2. Focus specifically on the Zig operation, i.e. a single right rotation.
3. Show:
   - the mathematical set of values (`view`) is unchanged,
   - the BST invariant is preserved,
   - the structure is correct: original left child becomes new root, original root becomes new right child.
4. No cheating via `sorry`, `admit`, empty bodies, or outsourcing the real work to existing verified library functions.

What the student implemented:
- A custom inductive `BinarySearchTree` with constructors `Empty` and `Node`.
- A custom `view` function computing the set of elements in the tree.
- A custom `is_bst` predicate expressing the BST ordering invariant recursively.
- A `zig` function:
  ```lean
  match t with
  | Node v (Node lv ll lr) r =>
      Node lv ll (Node v lr r)
  | _ => t
  ```
  This is exactly the standard single right rotation (zig): the left child becomes the new root, and the old root becomes the new right child, with the left child’s right subtree becoming the old root’s left subtree.

Why this matches the required algorithm:
- It is not some other implementation of set-preserving behavior; it is specifically the right rotation operation.
- The structure after rotation is exactly the expected one:
  - old left child root `lv` becomes root,
  - old root `v` becomes right child,
  - `ll` stays left subtree of `lv`,
  - `lr` becomes left subtree of old root `v`,
  - `r` remains right subtree of `v`.

About the proof obligations:
- The theorem `zig_postcond_satisfied` proves the postcondition for the implemented `zig`.
- The proof explicitly derives:
  - preservation of BST,
  - equality of `view`,
  - structural properties about new root and new right child.

Cheating check:
- No `sorry`, `admit`, or placeholders.
- `zig` is not empty and does real pattern matching / reconstruction.
- No use of pre-existing rotation or BST library implementation to avoid the work.
- No suspicious trick like defining `zig` arbitrarily and proving via inconsistent axioms.
- Imported `Mathlib`, but only standard set reasoning is used; the BST and zig are implemented from scratch.

Minor note:
- The fallback case `| _ => t` is irrelevant under the precondition, since the precondition ensures the root is a node with a left child that is also a node. So this is not a semantic issue.

Overall, the student implemented the correct zig rotation and proved the intended properties without obvious cheating.
